about: Builds proposed by Claude while this project was made with Claude Code. A proposal is a list of changes to the supplied Sierrathon design. Proposals are untrusted: only the Lean checker's verdict counts. Round 1 was written before Lean rated anything. Each later round was written after reading Lean's findings on the round before.

rounds.title: First ideas, before Lean has said anything

proposals.name: Keep it nominal
proposals.rationale: IPC-nominal land patterns everywhere and the manufacturer pattern for the flash: the safest choice for reflow assembly.

proposals.name: Thermal vias under the RP2040
proposals.rationale: Use KiCad's thermal-via QFN footprint so the exposed pad can dump heat into the inner planes.

proposals.name: Hand-solder the big passives
proposals.rationale: The 0603 and 0805 parts are the ones a person would rework by hand, so give only those the longer hand-solder pads.

proposals.name: Wider SOIC for the flash
proposals.rationale: KiCad's 5.275 mm SOIC-8 footprint also targets 208 mil bodies and has slightly longer pads.

proposals.name: Hand-solder the crystal
proposals.rationale: The 3225 crystal has pads under the body; the hand-solder footprint exposes them for an iron.

proposals.name: Hand-solder LEDs and regulator
proposals.rationale: LEDs are polarised and often replaced, and the regulator is the hottest part; longer pads make both easier to rework.

rounds.title: After reading Lean's findings on round 1

proposals.name: Nominal, with the paperwork fixed
proposals.rationale: Lean flagged the same three package problems on every round 1 build: BOM row 5 says 8 LEDs for 7 designators, the two documents disagree on inner copper, and 330 Ω needs the 8 mA pad setting. Fix those and keep nominal footprints.

proposals.name: No thermal-via footprint
proposals.rationale: Lean rejected the thermal-via QFN: its vias are drilled below the 8 mil minimum. Keep the plain QFN and let the exposed pad and planes carry the heat.

proposals.name: Hand-solder pads only where there is room
proposals.rationale: Lean showed the hand-solder crystal collides with R7, R13, R14 and R17. Keep the nominal crystal; use hand-solder pads only on the LEDs and the regulator, which Lean rated buildable.
